why: The LOCK on the template exclusion, which is what separates an escape hatch from a bypass. The marker only holds when its prefix is EXACTLY a known template root. On the pass side it is at new/site/blocks/ and the tree leaves the evaluation; on the fail side the same file is one level below, at new/site/blocks/app/, and it has to be REFUSED — the tree stays evaluated and the rule accuses. Without that lock, a modelo.json in any folder would hide any tree, which was exactly the three-byte attack the caso.json accepted once already.
